summary: 14-day telemetry reveals exceptional glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70–180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (< 70 mg/dL), an average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, and a low Coefficient of Variation of 12.9%. Active basal profiles, carb ratios, ISF values, and DIA (5.5 h) operate in high harmony with AAPS SMB/UAM automation and user meal strategies.

analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 CGM entries across 14 days representing 100.0% coverage with zero data gaps. 32 treatment entries and active profile parameters fully documented.
analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry data quality and profile completeness are excellent, supporting high-confidence analysis across all time windows.

analysis_steps.evidence: Mean glucose 117.0 mg/dL, SD 15.1 mg/dL, CV 12.9%, Time in Range 99.7%, Time Above Range 0.3%, Time Below Range 0.0%. Two isolated glucose readings near 70-71 mg/dL recorded overnight.
analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic profile demonstrates exceptional safety with negligible hypoglycemia risk and low overall variability.

analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight glucose averages 102.3–112.9 mg/dL between 00:00 and 06:00 local time. Basal segments (0.85–1.05 U/h) align with targets (90–115 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.findings: Basal delivery effectively maintains target glucose during fasting and overnight periods without autonomous drift.

analysis_steps.evidence: Postprandial returns to baseline occur reliably within 3–4 hours across 28 meal events. CR (9–12 g/U) and ISF (40–48 mg/dL/U) combined with DIA 5.5 h perform accurately.
analysis_steps.findings: Core profile parameters (CR, ISF, DIA) are accurately calibrated and prevent prolonged postprandial hyperglycemia or late hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.evidence: SMB and UAM enabled; 3 min delivery interval, 45 min max SMB basal, 30 min max UAM basal. Smooth glucose recovery following meal peaks without insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.findings: Automated micro-dosing efficiently assists meal boluses without driving glucose below target.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unpopulated boolean activation flags in raw export payload require verification on handset UI.

analysis_steps.evidence: Max basal rate 2.4 U/h (~2.3x highest scheduled basal rate), max IOB limit 8.0 U, dynamic ISF factor 100%.
analysis_steps.findings: Safety caps provide safe boundaries that allow effective automated response without risk of runaway insulin delivery.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens feature flags are unpopulated in export JSON.

analysis_steps.evidence: 28 logged meal boluses show an average 2-hour rise of +15 to +70 mg/dL depending on meal size, returning smoothly to baseline by hour 4.
analysis_steps.findings: User prebolus intervals (10–20 min) and split bolus strategies effectively dampen early postprandial spikes.

analysis_steps.evidence: Weekend brunch mixed-meal strategy (20g e-carbs over 120 min) correlates with stable 4–6 hour postprandial recovery (100–127 mg/dL at 6h).
analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs configuration accurately models extended absorption for high-fat/protein meals without generating excess residual COB.

analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesis across all 8 workflow stages confirms full alignment between profile parameters, automation settings, and observed glycemic telemetry.
analysis_steps.findings: No parameter changes are warranted. Primary action is maintaining current settings and verifying unpopulated UI feature flags on the handset.

strengths: Exceptional Time in Range of 99.7% (70–180 mg/dL) over 14 continuous days.
Zero Time Below Range (< 70 mg/dL: 0.0%) demonstrating excellent hypoglycemia safety.
Low glucose variability (CV 12.9%, SD 15.1 mg/dL) and stable mean glucose of 117.0 mg/dL.
100.0% CGM telemetry coverage with zero data gaps.
issues: Minor postprandial peak reaching 188 mg/dL during weekend brunches, which normalizes smoothly within 3–4 hours.

recommendations.title: Verify Handset UI Feature Flags
recommendations.description: Certain raw boolean flags (such as smb_always_enabled and autosens_enabled) appear as null in the export context. Confirm these settings directly in the AAPS app preferences on your phone.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current basal, CR, ISF, target, and DIA settings unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: 14-day telemetry confirms optimal glycemic outcomes (99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, mean 117 mg/dL, CV 12.9%). Scheduled basal and meal parameters are accurately calibrated.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Verify AAPS handset UI to ensure export artifacts (null booleans) reflect your intended preferences.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight glucose remains stable (avg 103-107 mg/dL) with zero hypoglycemia. Basal rate effectively maintains fasting baseline.
Morning fasting and pre-meal glucose values are stable without unexpected drift.
Afternoon glucose levels show strong baseline stability outside active postprandial windows.
Evening baseline glucose remains stable with smooth transition to night targets.
Midnight carb ratio is appropriate for late snacks or late meal recovery without causing hypoglycemia.
Weekday breakfast boluses achieved 100% TIR with average peak return to baseline within 3-4 hours.
Midday carb ratio accurately matches meal requirements for weekend brunches and lunch windows.
Dinner meal boluses result in predictable postprandial recovery (+15 to +41 mg/dL average 2-hour change) with 0.0% TBR.
Overnight correction responsiveness is appropriate and prevents over-correction lows.
Morning sensitivity factor safely manages corrections alongside active morning basal and meal boluses.
Afternoon ISF provides accurate correction response without driving glucose below target range.
Evening ISF is well-calibrated for evening meals and automatic SMB micro-boluses.
Overnight target range maintains stable glucose averaging 103-107 mg/dL.
Daytime target range supports strong TIR (99.7%) without increasing hypoglycemia risk.
Late night target provides a smooth transition into overnight rest with a safe target elevation.
5.5-hour DIA accurately models rapid-acting insulin decay and prevents insulin stacking across meal and SMB windows.
SMB and UAM are both active and functioning safely, maintaining 99.7% TIR with zero hypoglycemia.
Source activation condition booleans are null in the raw profile export; verify specific activation toggles directly on the AAPS handset UI.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: SMB delivery timing (3 min interval, 45 min max SMB basal, 30 min max UAM basal) provides effective postprandial dampening without over-delivery.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Safety limits (2.4 U/h max basal, 8.0 U max IOB) provide adequate headroom for postprandial automation while guarding against runaway delivery.
Autosens boolean feature flags are null in raw export; confirm feature settings on handset while dynamic ISF factor is set to a safe 100% neutral default.
Minimum carb impact (3 mg/dL/5 min) and max absorption duration (6 h) reliably model carbohydrate decay without premature COB truncation.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain current prebolus timing (15-20 min for fast carbs, 10 min for mixed meals) and 60-70% immediate bolus split, relying on AAPS SMB/UAM automation and e-carbs (20g over 120 min for weekend brunch) to manage extended absorption.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Meal response curves demonstrate excellent postprandial recovery across all 28 logged meal events with zero hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log exact prebolus administration timestamps in treatment records to evaluate if minor weekend brunch peaks (~188 mg/dL) can be further mitigated.

exceptions.suggestion: Use 10-minute prebolus, 60% immediate bolus, and 20g e-carbs over 120 min starting +15 min offset.
exceptions.rationale: Extends insulin coverage for high-fat/protein meal composition while SMB/UAM handles residual glucose rise.

exceptions.suggestion: Use 20-minute prebolus with 100% immediate bolus and no e-carbs.
exceptions.rationale: Fast-absorbing carbohydrate content completes absorption rapidly without requiring delayed insulin delivery.

implementation_steps: 1. Review current analysis results with your healthcare provider.
2. Confirm that all profile parameters (basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA, targets) remain unchanged as recommended.
3. Check the AAPS handset UI preferences menu to verify that unpopulated export flags (such as smb_always_enabled) match your intended active setup.
4. Continue monitoring glucose closely and maintaining consistent meal logging.
education: A 5.5-hour Duration of Insulin Action (DIA) aligns with physiological rapid-acting insulin tails and prevents insulin stacking during automated SMB delivery.
Using e-carbs (extended carbs) in AAPS helps the loop algorithm model extended fat and protein absorption without prematurely dropping calculated Carbs On Board (COB).
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice.
Independently verify all settings and consult your diabetes healthcare team before making therapy adjustments.
Always make parameter changes one at a time and monitor blood glucose closely for several days following any adjustment.
